description: VM-level resource investigation. What's wrong with this VM's resources?

links.title: Container Workbench
links.tooltip: Container resource consumption, lifecycle, per-service detail

panels.description: Worst-case 1m load average, normalized by vCPU count per host (load / core count). 1.0 = as busy as the host has cores; fleet is mixed (2 vCPU on core/monitoring, 4 vCPU on media/accelerated), so this scales fairly across all hosts instead of assuming 2 vCPUs everywhere.

targets.expr: max(node_load1{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"} / on(host) count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}) by (host))

panels.title: Load 1m

panels.description: Worst-case 5m load average, normalized by vCPU count per host (load / core count). 1.0 = as busy as the host has cores; fleet is mixed (2 vCPU on core/monitoring, 4 vCPU on media/accelerated), so this scales fairly across all hosts instead of assuming 2 vCPUs everywhere.

targets.expr: max(node_load5{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"} / on(host) count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}) by (host))

panels.title: Load 5m

panels.description: Worst-case 15m load average, normalized by vCPU count per host (load / core count). 1.0 = as busy as the host has cores; fleet is mixed (2 vCPU on core/monitoring, 4 vCPU on media/accelerated), so this scales fairly across all hosts instead of assuming 2 vCPUs everywhere.

targets.expr: max(node_load15{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"} / on(host) count(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}) by (host))

panels.title: Load 15m

panels.description: Worst-case swap usage across selected hosts. Any swap use means RAM was exhausted at some point.
panels.title: Swap Used

panels.description: Total OOM kill events across all selected hosts in the current time range. An OOM kill means the kernel terminated a process because memory was completely exhausted.
panels.title: OOM Kills

panels.description: Worst-case clock drift across selected hosts. High offset makes cross-VM log correlation unreliable.
panels.title: NTP Offset

panels.description: Average CPU time by mode across selected hosts. Shows where CPU time goes: user (app work), system (kernel), iowait (disk), steal (hypervisor contention). Note: when multiple hosts are selected, modes are averaged across all VMs — select a single host for accurate investigation.
panels.title: CPU by Mode

panels.description: Total CPU busy percentage per host. One line per VM — identifies which VM to focus on before the mode breakdown explains why.
panels.title: CPU % per Host

panels.description: Where RAM goes across selected hosts. Used = non-reclaimable (actual pressure). Cache = reclaimable by kernel on demand. Free = immediately available. Note: when multiple hosts are selected, values are averaged — select a single host for accurate investigation.
panels.title: Memory Composition

panels.description: Percentage of memory in use per host. Based on MemAvailable (accounts for reclaimable cache/buffers). One line per VM for comparing hosts with different RAM sizes.
panels.title: Memory Used %

panels.description: Swap bytes in use per host over time. Any swap use means RAM was exhausted at some point.
panels.title: Swap Usage

panels.description: Disk space used per mountpoint. Includes local and NFS mounts.

targets.expr: 1 - (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|btrfs|nfs|nfs4", mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|btrfs|nfs|nfs4", mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*"})

panels.title: Filesystem Usage

panels.description: Inode usage per mountpoint. Independent failure mode from disk space — small files can exhaust inodes while disk % stays low.

targets.expr: 1 - (node_filesystem_files_free{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|btrfs|nfs|nfs4", mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*"} / node_filesystem_files{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", fstype=~"ext4|xfs|btrfs|nfs|nfs4", mountpoint!~"/var/lib/docker/.*"})

panels.title: Inode Usage

panels.description: Read and write throughput per block device. Useful for finding which device is hot during high iowait.
panels.title: Disk I/O Rate

panels.description: Fraction of time each block device was busy. Values near 1.0 mean the device is saturated. Complements I/O Rate (how much) and I/O Latency (how slow).
panels.title: Disk I/O Utilization

panels.description: Average time per I/O operation per local block device (sda, sr0). Does NOT cover NFS mounts — node_exporter does not collect NFS client mountstats, so this panel has no visibility into NAS-side I/O latency. For NFS mount health, check the Filesystem Usage panel (is the mount reporting at all) and D03 Network (NAS TCP reachability).
panels.title: Disk I/O Latency

panels.description: Distinct directories over 1 GiB on this VM's local disk (node-exporter textfile collector; du -x, single filesystem, hourly). Roll-up parents (/, /var, /var/lib, /opt, per-stack config roots) are filtered out so each row is a distinct consumer — typically /var/lib/containerd (the Docker image store) plus any large per-service config bind mount. The '% of Disk' bar is the directory's share of the root filesystem total (see the Root Disk stat). Most app data lives on the NAS (NFS), which du -x does not walk. Empty until the node-exporter-textfile sidecar has run at least once.

targets.expr: (node_directory_size_bytes{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", path!~"/|/var|/var/lib|/opt|/var/lib/docker|/opt/self-hosting/docker_compose/[^/]+/config"} > 1073741824) / on(host) group_left() node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/", node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}

panels.title: Top Directories by Size

panels.description: Total size of this VM's root filesystem (/). Filesystem Usage shows used vs free; the Top Directories '% of Disk' bars are relative to this total.
panels.title: Root Disk

panels.description: Compact ranking of the top 15 containers on selected hosts by CPU usage. Click a service name to investigate in the Container Workbench.

targets.expr: sum by (host, service) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (host, service) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host", name!="", image!=""})

panels.title: Top 15 Containers by CPU

panels.description: Swap page-in/page-out rate per host. Separate from the Swap Used stat — this shows whether swapping is actively happening right now vs. a static amount sitting in swap.
panels.title: Swap Rate (pages/s)

panels.description: PSI 'some' pressure — fraction of time at least one task was stalled waiting on CPU, memory, or I/O. Non-zero pressure with normal-looking utilization is a saturation signal utilization alone misses.
panels.title: PSI Pressure (some)

panels.description: Conntrack table usage. If this hits 100%, new connections start getting dropped — relevant on media/core where NAT/proxy connection counts can spike.
panels.title: Conntrack Table Usage

panels.description: Open file descriptors as a fraction of the per-host limit. A container leaking FDs (or an NFS mount misbehaving) shows up here before anything else notices.

targets.expr: node_filefd_allocated{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"} / node_filefd_maximum{node=~"$node", vm_role=~"$vm_role", host=~"$host"}

panels.title: File Descriptor Usage

panels.description: TCP segments retransmitted per second. Sustained retransmits point at a lossy path (WAN edge, NFS over a congested link) rather than an application problem.
panels.title: TCP Retransmits

panels.description: eth0 throughput per host. Receive positive, transmit rendered negative so the chart centers at zero — same convention as the container network panel on D01b.
panels.title: eth0 Throughput
Extended Signals (swap rate, PSI, conntrack, fds, retransmits, eth0)
